 Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 20 points (8-of-11 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), 13 rebounds, six assists, one steal and three blocks in Monday’s win over the Rockets.
 While Antetokounmpo failed to score in the first quarter of Monday’s game, he did a bit of everything else. The Heat forward recorded eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and two blocks in the frame. Giannis scored six points in the second quarter and 14 in the third, extending his run of at least 20 points to 11 straight games. If Bam Adebayo (hip) misses time, Giannis will be even more important to the Heat than he already is. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Heat with 34 points (13-of-17 FGs), 14 rebounds, eight assists, one steal, three blocks and one three-pointer in a 137-117 win over the Pistons on Saturday. 
 Giannis wasn’t able to match his season high of 37 points that he set on Friday, but he was able to score at least 30 points for a third straight game, which led to Miami’s fourth straight win. Detroit didn’t have much of an answer for him, which helped him add an efficient shooting night to a dominant stat line. Plus, he was able to have an effective night at the free throw line, which helped inflate his value.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo had 37 points (15-of-20 FGs, 6-of-11 FTs), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and one three-pointer in the Heat’s 133-121 victory over the Cavaliers on Friday. 
 Antetokounmpo has scored at least 30 points in back-to-back games. This was his first game this month without double digit rebounds as he finished with only nine. Antetokounmpo and the Heat have won six of their last eight games after an 0-4 start to the season. They take on the Pistons at home on Saturday.

Myron Gardner gets his first start of the season with Andrew Wiggins remaining on the bench. Gardner has played 20 minutes this season with half of those minutes being played last game against the Jazz.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 30 points (12-of-21 FGs, 5-of-9 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Jazz. 
 Initially questionable for Tuesday’s game with a sprained right wrist, Antetokounmpo got up 21 shots against the Jazz. He scored 15 points in each half, shooting 7-of-14 from the field in the second half. Giannis’ dominant performance helped offset Bam Adebayo’s (11/8/4/4/2) 1-of-8 shooting from the field. The Heat head home, with a Friday/Saturday back-to-back against the Cavaliers and Pistons up next.

 LaMelo Ball struggled on Monday and finished with just six points (2-of-13 FGs), five rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers.
 While it didn’t prevent Minnesota from getting the win, this was LaMelo’s worst game of the season. He set a new season low for points and failed to dish out an assist for the first time this season. This was an uncharacteristically bad performance for him, especially compared to what he’s done in the month of November. He was held to 19 points in their previous game, which was his first time scoring less than 20 points this month. He’ll get back on track in Tuesday’s rematch with Portland.

 Rudy Gobert recorded a double-double on Monday with 18 points (5-of-10 FGs, 8-of-14 FTs), 15 rebounds, three assists and two blocks against the Trail Blazers.
 This was the fourth time this season that Gobert hauled in at least 15 rebounds, but he hasn’t had a scoring performance like this one. He set a new season high for scoring and scored in double figures for just the fourth time this season. Gobert’s still effective on the glass, and while he has improved as of late, he isn’t the shot blocker he once was. However, a huge dip in both field goal percentage and free throw percentage have really tanked his value.

 Terrence Shannon Jr. provided a boost off the bench with 34 points (8-of-11 FGs, 15-of-16 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 106-98 win over the Trail Blazers on Monday.
 With Anthony Edwards (knee) and Jaylen Clark (hamstring) sidelined, Shannon’s role has expanded in recent weeks. That led to him setting a new career high for scoring in this game, surpassing his previous mark of 33, which he set in April. Shannon is rostered in just 10 percent of Yahoo! leagues and should be a hot waiver wire pickup after this performance. However, managers should temper their expectations, unless he moves into the starting lineup.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Damian Lillard struggled on Monday and finished with just nine points (2-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, four assists, one block and two three-pointers against the Timberwolves.
 Lillard matched his season low for scoring in the loss, and he really just wasn’t able to get his shot going from anywhere. He shot 2-of-9 from deep and missed all six of his attempts inside the arc. This type of performance won’t happen often, though field goal percentage has been an issue for him all season, especially as of late. He’ll look to get back on track on Tuesday with a rematch in Minnesota.

 Deni Avdija led the Trail Blazers with 27 points (11-of-19 FGs), eight rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block, three three-pointers and five turnovers in a 106-98 loss to the Timberwolves on Monday.
 Avdija was productive in the first half of this game, entering the break with a game-high 21 points. However, he was only able to add six points after the break, which wasn’t enough to bring Portland back before he checked out with 7:28 left in the game. Avdija has had a strong season, and he has been red-hot lately, averaging 29.7 points and 3.3 triples over his last three games. They’ll remain in Minnesota for a rematch on Tuesday.

 Gui Santos (ankle) recorded 12 points (2-of-6 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Pelicans.
 After playing 21 minutes in Friday’s loss to the Spurs, Santos had one of his most productive outings of the season on Monday. The Warriors forward reached double figures for the third time this season and the first since October 26 against the Nuggets. Santos’ fantasy outlook isn’t good, even with Stephen Curry (oblique) out, especially as he continues to navigate lingering lower-body injuries. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Brandin Podziemski accounted for 15 points (3-of-8 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal, two blocks and three three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Pelicans.
 Limited to eight points in Friday’s blowout loss to the Spurs, Podziemski was more productive against the Pelicans. However, eight field-goal attempts are low for a player whose role grew in importance after Stephen Curry’s oblique injury. Hopefully, Podziemski will get up more shots in Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks.

 Yaxel Lendeborg finished Monday’s loss to the Pelicans with 28 points (9-of-23 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers.
 After a slow start, shooting 2-of-9 from the field, Lendeborg was more productive in the second half. The rookie forward shot 7-of-14 from the field and 4-of-4 from the foul line after halftime, scoring 20 points. With Stephen Curry (oblique) out for a few weeks, Lendeborg moves to the top of the offensive pecking order. That has negatively affected his efficiency, but Monday’s second-half performance was encouraging. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Derik Queen notched 17 points (6-of-9 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), 10 rebounds, one block and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Warriors.
 Queen’s double-double against the Warriors was his third of the season and first since October 28 against the Nuggets. While coming off the bench limits his fantasy ceiling, it hasn’t hurt Queen’s floor much. He’s been close to a top-100 player so far, and Queen has the skill set to maintain that production level for the rest of the season.
